summary: Among the supplied candidates, four documents directly apply graph neural network (GNN) message-passing methods to sepsis/septic deterioration prediction, and one applies a self-attention encoder to the same task. [V0003] (Chen et al., 2020) applies message passing over relational graphs to the LedgerGuard dataset, reporting 0.74 accuracy. [V0001] (Adebayo et al., 2018) applies the same GNN paradigm to the Atlas-ICU dataset, achieving AUROC 0.6. [V0002] (Brennan et al., 2019) evaluates message passing over relational graphs on AgriSat-4, reporting F1 of 0.67. [V0004] (Duarte et al., 2021) applies message passing over relational graphs to the CellLife dataset, with a reported MAE of 0.81. These four are the most directly relevant, as they combine the requested method (GNNs via message passing) with the requested topic (sepsis/septic deterioration prediction). [V0007] (Duarte et al., 2021) applies self-attention encoder models—not a GNN—to septic deterioration prediction on LedgerGuard (MAE 0.85), making it topically relevant but methodologically less aligned. All other candidates either address unrelated tasks (customer attrition, wildfire mapping, protein function, etc.) or use non-GNN methods on unrelated topics, and are therefore excluded.
